answer.short: The angles are not formed by the same two intersecting straight lines. $d=151^\circ$.

Angles on the straight line $SOQ$ sum to $180^\circ$.

content.prompt: How many degrees does the hour hand of a clock turn in:

answer.worked: The hour hand completes one full turn in 12 hours, so it turns $360^\circ$.

The hour hand completes two full turns in 24 hours.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Rotation}&=\frac{24}{12}\times360^\circ\\\text{Rotation}&=720^\circ\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Rotation}&=\frac{6}{12}\times360^\circ\\\text{Rotation}&=180^\circ\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Rotation}&=360^\circ\div12\\\text{Rotation}&=30^\circ\end{align*}$$

The hour hand turns $30^\circ$ in 60 minutes.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Rotation}&=\frac{30}{60}\times30^\circ\\\text{Rotation}&=15^\circ\end{align*}$$

The hour hand turns $30^\circ$ in 60 minutes.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Rotation}&=30^\circ\div60\\\text{Rotation}&=0.5^\circ\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: Suppose $\angle ABC$ is obtuse. What type of angle is $\angle DEF$, given that $\angle ABC=2\angle DEF$?

answer.worked:
Since $\angle ABC$ is obtuse, $90^\circ<\angle ABC<180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABC&=2\angle DEF\\\angle DEF&=\frac{\angle ABC}{2}\end{align*}$$
Dividing the bounds by $2$ gives $45^\circ<\angle DEF<90^\circ$.
Therefore $\angle DEF$ is acute.

answer.worked:
Clockwise from 12, the hour hand moves $30^\circ$ per hour and $0.5^\circ$ per minute; the minute hand moves $6^\circ$ per minute.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Hour-hand angle} &= 10\times30^\circ+10\times0.5^\circ\\\text{Hour-hand angle} &= 305^\circ\\\text{Minute-hand angle} &= 10\times6^\circ\\\text{Minute-hand angle} &= 60^\circ\\\text{Separation} &= 305^\circ-60^\circ\\\text{Separation} &= 245^\circ\\\text{Smaller angle} &= 360^\circ-245^\circ\\\text{Smaller angle} &= 115^\circ\end{align*}$$

Measure both hand positions clockwise from 12.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Hour-hand angle} &= 4\times30^\circ+45\times0.5^\circ\\\text{Hour-hand angle} &= 142.5^\circ\\\text{Minute-hand angle} &= 45\times6^\circ\\\text{Minute-hand angle} &= 270^\circ\\\text{Smaller angle} &= 270^\circ-142.5^\circ\\\text{Smaller angle} &= 127.5^\circ\end{align*}$$

Measure both hand positions clockwise from 12.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Hour-hand angle} &= 7\times30^\circ+15\times0.5^\circ\\\text{Hour-hand angle} &= 217.5^\circ\\\text{Minute-hand angle} &= 15\times6^\circ\\\text{Minute-hand angle} &= 90^\circ\\\text{Smaller angle} &= 217.5^\circ-90^\circ\\\text{Smaller angle} &= 127.5^\circ\end{align*}$$

Measure both hand positions clockwise from 12.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Hour-hand angle} &= 2\times30^\circ+35\times0.5^\circ\\\text{Hour-hand angle} &= 77.5^\circ\\\text{Minute-hand angle} &= 35\times6^\circ\\\text{Minute-hand angle} &= 210^\circ\\\text{Smaller angle} &= 210^\circ-77.5^\circ\\\text{Smaller angle} &= 132.5^\circ\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: Prove that $AB\parallel CD$.

spec.description: Unfilled quadrilateral ABDC; AC extends past C. Only BD and AC carry rightward parallel arrows. No angle arcs.
spec.mathematics: BD parallel AC; angle ABD = 125 degrees; exterior angle at C = 55 degrees. Coordinates use a freely chosen drawing scale consistent with these angles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens; no AB/CD parallel marks.

answer.short: $AB\parallel CD$, since the co-interior angles sum to $180^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$\angle BDC=55^\circ$ (alternate angles, $BD\parallel AC$).
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABD+\angle BDC&=125^\circ+55^\circ\\\angle ABD+\angle BDC&=180^\circ\end{align*}$$
Therefore $AB\parallel CD$ (converse of the co-interior angle theorem).

spec.description: Triangle AEB with C on AE, D on EB and internal segment CD. Embedded triangle CDE belongs to this same figure. No parallel marks or angle arcs.
spec.mathematics: Angle EAB = 45 degrees; angle AEB = 100 degrees; exterior angle CDB = 145 degrees. Drawn using base length 4.6 arbitrary units, apex at the intersection of rays at 45 and 145 degrees. CD endpoints share height; this placement does not add a printed parallel assertion.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABE&=180^\circ-45^\circ-100^\circ\\\angle ABE&=35^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles in triangle $ABE$. Since $B,D,E$ are collinear, $\angle DBA=35^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle CDB+\angle DBA&=145^\circ+35^\circ\\\angle CDB+\angle DBA&=180^\circ\end{align*}$$
Therefore $AB\parallel CD$ (converse of the co-interior angle theorem).

content.prompt: Find the value of $\theta$.

spec.description: Open zigzag between upper and lower rightward horizontal arms. Both horizontal arms carry leftward parallel arrows. Vertices are unlabelled. No angle arcs are supplied.
spec.mathematics: Internal coordinate names U,V,W,X are not printed. From V, VU has direction 70 degrees and VW direction -50 degrees. From W, WX has direction 225 degrees. Thus the angle at U is 110 degrees, the reflex angle at V is 240 degrees, and the left-opening angle at W is 95 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Retain 110 degrees, reflex 240 degrees, 95 degrees and theta only. Construction lines and derived angles are solution-only.

answer.worked:
Construct horizontal lines through both intermediate bends, parallel to the marked lines.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-110^\circ\\\alpha&=70^\circ\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles on parallel lines.
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=360^\circ-240^\circ\\\beta&=120^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles at a point.
$$\begin{align*}\gamma&=120^\circ-70^\circ\\\gamma&=50^\circ\end{align*}$$
The angle at the next bend is also $50^\circ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).
$$\begin{align*}\delta&=95^\circ-50^\circ\\\delta&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$
$\theta=45^\circ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

content.prompt: $AB$ is parallel to $CD$. Prove that $WY$ is parallel to $XZ$.

spec.description: Horizontal lines A–W–X–B and C–Y–Z–D have one right-pointing parallel mark each. Oblique segments WY and XZ have no parallel marks. Non-reflex sectors BXZ, WYZ and XZD carry 7a, 3(a + 10) and 5a respectively, without degree symbols. All regions remain unfilled.
spec.mathematics: AB is parallel to CD. The upper and lower horizontal lines have collinear point orders A,W,X,B and C,Y,Z,D. The marked angles at X and Z are co-interior. The marked angles at Y and Z are corresponding for the two oblique lines. Coordinates reproduce schematic placement and are not additional givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no calculated values or parallel marks on WY and XZ.

answer.short: $WY\parallel XZ$, since $\angle WYZ=\angle XZD=75^\circ$ (equal corresponding angles).
answer.worked:
Since $AB\parallel CD$, co-interior angles sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}5a+7a&=180\\12a&=180\\a&=15\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\angle WYZ&=3(a+10)\\&=3(15+10)\\&=75^\circ\\\angle XZD&=5a\\&=5(15)\\&=75^\circ\end{align*}$$
Therefore $WY\parallel XZ$, because corresponding angles are equal.

inlines.text: Show working to explain how you know.

spec.description: Straight segments A–B–C and D–E–F slope gently down to the right. A diagonal transversal rises through E and B and extends past both intersections. Adjacent sectors ABE and EBC below ABC are labelled (5x + 6)° and (16x + 6)°. Sector DEB above DEF is labelled (20x − 15)°. No parallel marks or shading.
spec.mathematics: A,B,C are collinear and D,E,F are collinear. The transversal contains E and B. Angles ABE and EBC form a straight angle. No parallelism is given. Coordinates reproduce the schematic source, not measured angle values.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the three supplied angle expressions and point labels are visible.

answer.worked:
Angles on straight line $ABC$ sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}(5x+6)+(16x+6)&=180\\21x+12&=180\\21x&=168\\x&=8\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\angle EBC&=(16\times8+6)^\circ\\&=134^\circ\\\angle DEB&=(20\times8-15)^\circ\\&=145^\circ\end{align*}$$
The alternate angles are unequal. Therefore $ABC$ is not parallel to $DEF$.

entries.description: Two separate straight segments slope gently down to the right: A–B–C above D–E–F. A steeper diagonal transversal rises from lower left to upper right through E and B, extending beyond both intersections to unlabelled endpoints. No parallel markings are present. At B, an arc in the sector between BA and BE marks ∠ABE as (5x + 6)°. An adjacent arc between BE and BC marks ∠EBC as (16x + 6)°. These two angles occupy the half-plane below ABC and form a straight angle. At E, an arc above DEF between ED and EB marks ∠DEB as (20x − 15)°. All marked angles are non-reflex. Labels: A, B, C, D, E, F, (5x + 6)°, (16x + 6)°, (20x − 15)°. No lengths, right-angle marks, equal-angle marks or shading are supplied. Apparent similarity of line directions is not a given of parallelism.
